_why_two_claims: AGREEMENT asks whether the engines compute the same thing; RECOVERY asks whether they compute the right thing. Neither implies the other.

truth.source: the fixture's data-generating process: risk = 0.10 + 0.08 x treated + 0.004 x (age - 60)

agreement.claim: both engines report the same risk difference, standard error, interval and age slope
agreement._note: Observed spread on the committed fixture: up to 1.6e-7, with both fits at tolerance 1e-12. At R's default glm epsilon (1e-8) the two stopped 1.05e-5 apart, which is why the tolerance is pinned in both files. harness/regression_examples.test.py checks the estimate against a direct Nelder-Mead maximization of the binomial likelihood and shows the logit link's coefficient (0.83) is a different quantity.

recovery.claim: the adjusted risk difference and age slope are close to the fixture's

calibration.rule: about 1.3 times the measured 99th percentile miss, rounded up
calibration.limits: Measured by harness/regression_examples.test.py over seeds 0 to 99 of this generator.
